Key points
• The switch between cuprous and cupric states underpins the metal’s essentiality in systemic substrate metabolism, energy
production, tissue synthesis, neurotransmission and peptide endocrine activity.
• Elements of its roles and homeostasis are evolutionarily conserved thus enabling a systems biology approach to studying its
essentialty.
• Reference intakes of copper for adults approximate 1.0-1.5 mg daily. It is widely distributed in the diet particularly in cereals
and grains.
• The liver is the main regulator of systemic metabolism and homeostasis of copper by means of its seqestration with cysteine
rich isoproteins, collectively called metallthionein.
• Two inborn errors of copper metabolism affecting its systemic distribution from the liver (Menkes Disease) and its biliary
excretion (Wilson Disease) have highlighted the affects of low and high body burdens of copper.
